I, Nick Feamster, Ph.D, declare under penalty of perjury, pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1746, as follows:
1. I submit this Declaration in support of OpenAI Defendants’ (collectively, “OpenAT’)
Motion for Summary Judgment.

A. Professional Background and Qualifications

2. I am the Neubauer Professor of Computer Science and the Founding Director of the Center
for Data and Computing (now the Data Science Institute) at the University of Chicago, where I
have served as a full professor since July 2019. I previously served as a computer science professor
at Princeton University and the Georgia Institute of Technology.

3. My work includes extensive research on web technologies, Internet protocols, and how
web applications behave under different network conditions. I have also researched how web

crawlers and bots operate and how websites implement access restrictions. This research includes

4. I also have extensive practical experience with the technical and operational aspects of web
crawling. I was an employee and lead technical engineer at LookSmart, an early search engine
company, where I designed and wrote LookSmart’s first web crawler and indexer in 1997. In this
role, I designed crawler architecture to discover and retrieve web content efficiently, implemented
robots.txt parsing and compliance processes designed to respect website owner preferences,
and handled HTTP protocol interactions, user agent identification, and server responses. Through
this experience I obtained a first-hand understanding of engineering decisions involved in
operating web crawlers and fundamental principles of web crawling, including transparent crawler
identification and respecting robots.txt.

5. I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
(MIT) in 2005. My doctoral research developed new methods to analyze and predict the behavior
of large-scale Internet routing systems, focusing on ensuring that networks route traffic correctly
and predictably. I also earned an undergraduate degree in Electrical Engineering and Computer
Science and a Master’s degree in Computer Science from MIT in 2000 and 2001 respectively.

issues and standard practices related to web crawling, the technical operation and widespread
acceptance of the Robots Exclusion Protocol (REP) via robots.txt files, and website operator
norms related to other Internet technologies relevant to this case. I was also asked to provide
opinions regarding whether OpenAI’s Browse functionality operates in a manner consistent with

these widely accepted practices, protocols, and norms.

9. Retrieval Augmented Generation or “RAG” is an AI-based capability that combines a large
language model (LLM) with external information retrieval tools. A RAG-enabled LLM can
retrieve relevant information from sources external to the LLM’ s training data, such as the Internet,
using automated retrieval techniques.

underlying ChatGPT to search the web and retrieve information before generating an answer to a
user query.!

ChatGPT conversation records provided to me by OpenAI. These records contain conversation

transcripts along with their associated metadata, including fields reflecting operational events not
